metadata.title: Mid-60s Comic Strip Pop Album Cover

recipe.visualDefinition: A vibrant, multi-panel comic-style layout featuring a large, stylized female character on the left with arms raised, interacting with the main title, set against a grid of four narrative panels with hand-drawn textures and saturated primary colors.
coreVisualRelationships: Large character on left acts as a vertical anchor and interacts with the arched title
Four-quadrant grid on the right provides narrative density
Hand-drawn black outlines unify disparate color blocks
Textured, gritty backgrounds contrast with flat character fills

compositionAndHierarchy.subjectPositionAndScale: Primary character occupies the left third, standing full-height; four narrative panels occupy the remaining two-thirds in a 2x2 grid.
compositionAndHierarchy.visualAnchor: The large character's raised hands which appear to 'hold' the arched title text.
compositionAndHierarchy.movementAndEyePath: Starts at the arched title, follows the character down, then moves clockwise through the four comic panels.
compositionAndHierarchy.negativeSpace: Minimal; the composition is densely packed with illustration and text, using the off-white background as a separator.

colorSystem.dominantColorRole: Off-white background provides a neutral base for high-energy colors.
colorSystem.contrastColorRole: Heavy black ink outlines define all shapes and characters.
colorSystem.accentColorRole: Saturated yellow, orange, and red provide high-key focal points within panels.
colorSystem.saturationAndValueRelationship: High saturation across all hues with a consistent mid-to-dark value range in the ink work.
paletteRestrictions: Limit to a 1960s printing gamut (CMYK-like primaries)

typographyAndGraphicLanguage.baseSkeleton: Heavy slab serif and blocky sans-serif
letterConstructionRules: Arched baseline for the main title
characterSpecificRedesigns: Letters in the main title are slightly rotated to follow the curve
typographyAndGraphicLanguage.pairingStrategy: Pair the arched display title with a secondary blocky sans-serif for credits and smaller script or sans for panel captions.

candidateDirections.reason: Captures the irregular, mid-century cut-out look
Provides the necessary weight and rounded terminals

twoStageComposition.backgroundInstruction: Generate a 1960s style comic illustration on off-white paper. On the left, a tall, quirky girl with blonde hair and a bright orange jacket stands with arms raised. On the right, a 2x2 grid of comic panels showing various characters in urban settings with vibrant red, yellow, and blue fills. Use heavy black ink outlines and a slightly weathered texture.
twoStageComposition.overlayInstruction: Add the main title in a heavy, hand-drawn black slab serif font, arched across the top so the girl's hands appear to touch the letters. Add secondary text in a bold blocky sans-serif below the arch.

verificationChecks: Does the line work have a hand-inked quality?
Are the colors saturated and primary-focused?
Is the layout split between a main character and a panel grid?

mustRedesign: Specific character faces to avoid likenesses

mustAchieve: Dynamic interaction between text and character
Cohesive hand-drawn style across all elements

postGenerationChecks: Ensure no text is 'floating' without stylistic integration
Check that ink outlines are consistent in weight
Verify the off-white background isn't too bright or sterile
Confirm the character on the left is the primary visual anchor
recipe.reuseFormula: Combine [Quirky Character Illustration] + [Arched Hand-Drawn Display Type] + [Multi-Panel Comic Grid] + [1960s Primary Palette].
